MovieScript:
Years later, the weight of the world had only grown heavier. The secret had nearly been exposed when the school bus went off the bridge. Clark had pulled the bus from the river, saving every child—including Pete Ross, the boy who used to bully him.

In the quiet of the Kent barn, the air was thick with the scent of hay and the cold reality of the truth. Jonathan Kent stood before his son, his face a map of worry and love.

"What was I supposed to do?" Clark asked, his voice trembling with a mix of defiance and fear. "Just let them die?"

Jonathan looked at the ground, a long silence stretching between them. "Maybe," he said softly. It wasn't cruelty; it was terror. "There’s more at stake here than just our lives, Clark. When the world finds out what you can do, it’s going to change everything. People are afraid of what they don't understand."

He led Clark to a tarp-covered object hidden beneath the floorboards. Beneath the cloth sat a craft of jagged, alien geometry—the vessel that had brought him to Earth. Jonathan handed him a small, metallic key, cold to the touch and etched with symbols that felt ancient.

"You're the answer, son," Jonathan said, placing a heavy hand on Clark's shoulder. "You're the answer to 'Are we alone in the universe?'"

"I don't want to be," Clark whispered.

"I don't blame you. It’s a huge burden. But you were sent here for a reason. One day, you’ll have to make a choice: whether to stand proud in front of the human race or not."

Clark looked at the man who had raised him. "Can't I just keep pretending I'm your son?"

Jonathan’s eyes welled with tears as he pulled him into a hug. "You are my son. But you owe it to yourself to find out who gave you that other name, and why."
